captions.detailed: A Nordic-style wooden stave bell tower featuring a dark brown timber-frame shaft with diagonal cross-braces, vertical slats at the base, and an open belfry at the top. It is crowned by a dark-shingled pitched roof topped with a simple wooden cross. Inside the belfry, a single dark cast-iron bell is suspended, supported by a horizontal wooden yoke that pivots on a revolute joint, allowing the bell to swing back and forth.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a Nordic wooden stave bell tower with a square timber-frame shaft, vertical slats on the lower half, diagonal bracing, and a pitched roof topped with a cross. Inside the open belfry, hang a dark metal bell from a wooden yoke using a revolute joint so it can swing freely.
captions.factory: Construct the tower base and frame by combining vertical and horizontal timber beams (Box primitives) with diagonal cross-braces. Create the lower enclosure using an array of vertical slats. Build the pitched roof from angled plates (Box primitives) and add a simple cross on top. Model the bell using a combination of revolved profiles or cylinders, and attach it to a horizontal yoke. Define a revolute joint between the top timber frame and the yoke to allow rotation around the horizontal pitch axis.
